judgements.justification: A's AC rejected because the MMD and KCpA comparison and kernel experiments existed only as rebuttal promises ('should not happen in the authors' response'), while B accepted with the same gaps.
B's only detractor, Reviewer_hFCk, wrote 'I now lean to accept' but never edited its 5, and B accepted with a spotlight as if no reviewer opposed.
Neither committee's AC called in an extra reviewer; both decisions rest on the reviews on the record.
Clarity was not a dividing issue; both committees' objections concern novelty, experiments and assumptions, not exposition read differently by expertise.
A's pviK raised 5 to 6 with a stated reason ('in light of some of your other comments'), and A rejected anyway; no B reviewer raised a score.
No AC discounted a silent detractor; A's silent MgSk and B's silent 5aeA both rated at or above threshold.
B's only rating above 7, W1jH's 8, came from a 3-hour review that misread novelty and detection performance, not a detailed checked reading.
No reviewer in either committee admitted reading only part of the paper.
Both committees judged the paper within its own kernel change-point framing; no reviewer contested the premise from another theoretical tradition.
B's meta-review, though three sentences, states a case for high merit ('great scholarly work, from its writing to empirical demonstrations') rather than arguing only for acceptance.
Both committees knew the related literature: B's ZPrG and 5aeA saw the Vogt special case and the MMD link, as A's Rm3m and pviK did.
The notes record no misstatement of reviewers' final positions in either meta-review; A's AC drew its demands accurately from pviK and Rm3m.
No reviewer or AC in either committee raised narrow audience or a better-suited venue.
B's lone detractor hFCk made correct checkable points, not misreadings, and B's chair gave a spotlight rather than arguing only acceptance.
A's rebuttal offered explanations and promises, not new experimental results shown to one committee only.
A's most confident reviewer Rm3m rated lowest (5), and B's most confident W1jH rated highest and the chair followed it; no expert was outweighed upward.
No reviewer added a new objection after the response period; pviK's 2021-09-10 edit raised its score.
A's reviewers raised additional real experimental gaps (untuned kernels, no type I error, no real-data baselines), so their assessments were less favourable, not equal at a harsher scale.
B's hFCk judged the generality claim overstated, yet B gave the higher tier; A did not raise the claim and rejected on missing comparisons.
A's 6s led to rejection over missing comparisons, not a poster from flat scores, and no A reviewer said it could not check the technical core.
